Chapter 6467: No Different From Insects

Chapter 6467: No Different From Insects

Alch-deer was a creature from Desolate Frontier that reached the dao. Everything about his cultivation originated from his sect. However, there was no hint of Desolate Frontier in his power.

The other primal ancestors couldn’t do the same. Their moves and power source had traces of their original dao. The most apparent was the Buddhist influence in Rising’s techniques.

As for Alch-deer, he looked like a native of Gold Village, the very original one. As he raised his hands, he seemingly forgot his origin and became a part of the village.

“No wonder he achieved so much here.” Ocean-gaze couldn’t help but praise.

Once people saw him in action, they couldn’t help but forget his true cultivation. The village seemed to be alive and rotated around him.

Everyone felt the village becoming larger after his “wish” despite him not being its creator. This was their desire as well since they wanted this place to become an independent realm.

“Rumble!” He overcame both attacks.

People were sent flying in the air while Rising and Earthsplitter staggered backward. Once they stabilized, blood streamed down the corners of their lips.

They were undoubtedly weaker than Alch-deer despite working together.

“The lord of Gold Village.” Everyone became emotional.

Every emperor and desolate god present was stronger than Alch-deer in the real world. The only exception was Black Wind Monarch. Alas, they saw just how unbeatable he was in Gold Village.

“You lost.” He spoke overbearingly while the natives kowtowed to worship him.

Earthsplitter and Rising exchanged glances.

“We lost.” Rising accepted and said: “But killing us won’t be easy.”

Alch-deer paused for a moment before nodding: “Yes, destroying a primal anima is difficult.”

Despite his incredible boost in power, his true cultivation remained limited while they had a primal anima.

Its toughness couldn’t be understated. Primal ancestors had a hard time killing each other, let alone someone without.

“You two are no different than insects.” Li Qiye interjected.

The crowd gasped and whispered among themselves.

“Is this true?” A desolate god asked softly.

“Stand back.” Li Qiye told Alch-deer.

“Yes, Ancestor.” Alch-deer bowed and stood behind him.

Li Qiye finally got out of his chair and stretched. All eyes were on him because this was someone above primal ancestors. His comment was far from outrageous given his current followers.
